newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crude offerings steady in U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crude offerings steady in U.S. markets.

text.p: Foreign crude offerings into the U.S. Gulf were mostly steady from Tuesday, with most markets talked but not traded actively.
Traders said continued narrowing in the June spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent moved to $1.45-$1.55 from a $1.60 value late Tuesday
Still, traders said a European player was showing Brent for early June delivery at June WTI -70 cents, steady from Tuesday talk.
Nigerian Brass River was also on offer for early June, pegged at an asking price of Dated Brent +$2.05.
West African talk also had a European firm showing the same 950,000 barrel cargo of Nigerian Bonny Light from Tuesday, for late May arrival in the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP).
Traders said the asking prices was around 15-20 cents a barrel from a former discount of around minus 37 cents.
Foreign players eyed a trend Wednesday for increased demand for foreign barrels.
"Generally, there has been a slight increase in demand," said a Gulf trader, noting phone activity had accelerated even if new trades had not been sealed.
Latin American discussion was quiet, with no fresh word on the Chilean state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) tendering for 960,000 barrels of crude for June 25-30.
"There was not movement in the Latin American grades, it seemed like a Monday on a Wednesday," said a Houston trader.
